assertions.description: An organiser holding the event-update capability can POST events.landing.share and the resulting link renders the DRAFT event's landing preview to an unauthenticated visitor (HTTP 200, event content present, visitor stays a guest, event state unchanged).
A share link whose parameters were stripped, injected into, or altered is refused rather than served — the link must be tamper-evident, not merely a guessable permanent URL.
A link that worked when minted stops serving the landing content long after issue (checked 400 days later), proving the link is genuinely time-limited rather than permanent.
A link issued for one event neither renders another event's content nor grants access when re-pointed at a second event or when a second event's link is grafted with the first link's credentials.
Minting is refused for a team member that holds only the event-view capability, for an organiser of another workspace, and for an unauthenticated visitor — no usable link is produced by any of them.

The shared read-only rendering contains no write form targeting the public registration submission route and no target pointing at the authenticated landing editor, authenticated landing preview, or publish endpoint.
After opening a valid share link the visitor is still a guest, and the authenticated landing editor and landing preview routes remain refused and render no event content for that visitor.

With a share link live, the DRAFT event is still refused on the permanent public landing route and its landing content is not served there — the private-DRAFT invariant is not widened to enable sharing.
